submission.justification: Absorber-F3 gives the best 100 GeV electron energy resolution in every thickness I simulated. The minimum lies between 4 and 5 mm: 4 mm gave 3.177% and 5 mm gave 3.194%, a difference that is within the likely run-to-run noise, so 4 mm is recommended. For comparison, the best F1 point was 3.82% (5 mm) and the best F2 point was 5.11% (5 mm). Thicker or thinner plates were worse for F3 (2 mm: 3.75%, 3 mm: 3.47%, 6 mm: 3.44%, 8 mm: 3.74%). Cooling, readout and mechanical support are documented as compatible with all three candidates, so they do not separate the options. No project document quantifies hands-on maintenance access for any absorber, so that constraint could not be verified from the documents; it is flagged as unknown for the recommended option.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three materials in candidate_specs.md

requirements.evidence: F3 at 4 mm: 3.177%, the lowest of all simulated points (F1 best 3.816%, F2 best 5.11%). F3 at 5 mm: 3.194%.

No document addresses maintenance access or activation for any absorber. Meeting notes say mechanical support is compatible with all candidates, which does not confirm maintenance access. Needs verification before final design.
